Maya includes every point on the line segment; Eli includes only points permitted by the booking rule. First write the original domain and range as sets, then justify which model represents valid bookings. Next, the venue changes its rule to allow any real number of hours from 1 through 4, including the endpoints, while keeping the same fee relationship. Determine the revised minimum and maximum costs, predict the cost of a 2.5-hour booking, and justify why that booking becomes valid under the revised model.
questions.scenario: An equipment kit costs a fixed $2 booking fee plus $1 per hour. Originally, customers may book only 1, 2, 3, or 4 whole hours. Let x be the booked hours and y be the total cost in dollars. The table lists the original bookings. The line segment shows the fee relationship for every real value of x from 1 through 4; decide which plotted points actually fit each booking policy.

answerFields.label: Which argument justifies the valid original model?
options: Eli is correct: the whole-hour booking rule restricts the domain, so only the permitted points on the line describe bookings.
Maya is correct: drawing a continuous line automatically makes every fractional-hour booking available.
Eli is correct only because a straight line cannot represent fractional input values.
Both are incorrect because paying a fixed fee makes the relation fail to be a function.
answerFields.answer: Eli is correct: the whole-hour booking rule restricts the domain, so only the permitted points on the line describe bookings.
